elements.reason: The abstract text does not explicitly identify the report as a 'systematic review', although it describes systematic review methods.

elements.quote: Objective To assess the effects of waiting time for outpatient psychotherapeutic interventions on patient-reported outcomes in adolescents and adults with eating disorders.
elements.reason: The abstract explicitly states the main objective.

elements.quote: Quantitative studies of adolescents (≥ 10 years) and adults with eating disorders that examined waitlist conditions prior to outpatient psychotherapeutic interventions and measured eating disorder pathology with the Children's Eating Attitudes Test (chEAT) or Eating Disorder Examination-Questionnaire (EDE-Q) were eligible.
elements.reason: The abstract specifies inclusion criteria for studies and participants.

elements.quote: Method MEDLINE, Embase, APA PsycInfo, CENTRAL and BASE were searched on 12 August 2025.
elements.reason: The abstract identifies information sources and the search date.

elements.quote: Risk of bias was assessed using the RoB 2 and ROBINS-I tools.
elements.reason: The abstract specifies the tools used to assess risk of bias.

elements.quote: A within-group random-effects meta-analysis was performed assessing pre-post change scores of the EDE-Q Global Score (primary analysis) and EDE-Q subscales (secondary analyses).
elements.reason: The abstract specifies the methods used to synthesize results.

elements.quote: Results Nine waitlist-controlled studies (total n = 647, waitlisted n = 283) including adult participants with bulimia nervosa, binge-eating disorder and 'eating disorder not otherwise specified' met our eligibility criteria.
elements.reason: The abstract reports the number of included studies and participants and summarizes characteristics.

elements.quote: Eight studies (waitlisted n = 273) were included in the meta-analysis. ... The pooled pre-post effect estimate was Hedges' g = - 0.17 (95% CI - 0.30 to - 0.05), indicating a negligible reduction in eating disorder pathology.
elements.reason: The abstract presents results for the main outcomes with effect estimates.

elements.quote: The pooled pre-post effect estimate was Hedges' g = - 0.17 (95% CI - 0.30 to - 0.05)
elements.reason: The abstract reports the summary estimate and confidence interval for the meta-analysis.
The abstract describes a within-group meta-analysis of waitlist control groups, not a comparison between different intervention groups.

elements.quote: Certainty of evidence was rated as moderate, given the high risk of bias across studies.
elements.reason: The abstract summarizes limitations regarding risk of bias.

elements.quote: Discussion Based on our results, waiting in waitlist control groups represents a period during which substantial eating disorder pathology and associated distress persist without therapeutic intervention.
elements.reason: The abstract provides a general interpretation of the results.
The abstract does not specify the primary source of funding for the review.

elements.quote: A full protocol has been preregistered on PROSPERO (registration number: CRD420251090691).
elements.reason: The abstract provides the register name and registration number.

elements.quote: The research question 'What are the effects of waiting time for outpatient psychotherapeutic interventions on PROs in adolescents and adults with AN, BN, BED and OSFED' was formulated using the Population, Exposure, Comparator, Outcome (PECO) framework (Additional file 1).
elements.reason: The manuscript explicitly states the research question and confirms it was formulated using the PECO framework.

elements.quote: The research question 'What are the effects of waiting time for outpatient psychotherapeutic interventions on PROs in adolescents and adults with AN, BN, BED and OSFED' was formulated using the Population, Exposure, Comparator, Outcome (PECO) framework (Additional file 1).
elements.reason: The review addresses intervention effects (waiting time for psychotherapeutic interventions) and explicitly states the planned comparisons using the PECO framework.

elements.quote: Studies were included if they used an empirical, quantitative design, either randomised or non-randomised, such as RCTs, clinical trials, quasi-experimental studies or cohort studies; involved adolescents (≥ 10 years, according to the World Health Organization [72] definition) and/or adults (≥ 18 years) with AN, BN, BED or OSFED... compared an active psychotherapeutic intervention group (IG) in an outpatient setting with a WLCG or a no-treatment control group... reported these PROs for a minimum of two time points: (1) at or near the time of initial consultation... (baseline), and (2) at least once at a subsequent time point
elements.reason: The eligibility criteria section explicitly specifies study designs, participant characteristics (age, diagnosis), settings (outpatient), and follow-up requirements (minimum two time points).

elements.quote: Studies were included regardless of publication status. Both peer-reviewed and grey literature were considered. No restrictions were applied regarding publication year or language.
elements.reason: The document explicitly states that publication status, year, and language had no restrictions, satisfying the requirement to specify report characteristics.

The retrieved evidence does not contain a statement distinguishing between exclusion due to outcomes not being measured versus outcomes not being reported within the eligibility criteria or methods sections.

elements.quote: Nine waitlist-controlled studies (total n = 647, waitlisted n = 283) including adult participants with bulimia nervosa, binge-eating disorder and 'eating disorder not otherwise specified' met our eligibility criteria. elements.quote: Rationales for the exclusion criteria are provided in Additional file 3.

elements.quote: Corresponding study authors were contacted if WLCG mean values or SDs of the EDE-Q Global Score or subscales for the two mandatory time points were missing. For Arcelus et al. [104], post-waiting means and post-waiting SDs were unavailable and could not be obtained by contacting the corresponding author. Post-waiting means were derived by adding the reported mean difference (MD) to the pre-waiting mean. As proposed by Morris [105] and Morris and DeShon [106], SDs in pre- and post-test populations can be assumed equal. However, to increase the precision we approximated post-waiting SDs by multiplying the pre-waiting SD by the average proportional change in SDs from pre to post observed in the remaining included studies.
